{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ne-o","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"bb3798efc1488945e4265c2ff76c0031714b48c971852947b3f927100e9d233c","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ne-class-o:lineage:62","source_registry_sha256":"66161d94cc863d3cf353417f54f101bf8681de71fc4c3b73f43c86f2be1c7398","source_liveness_sha256":"78587b1f8f8617c7b8b0a43b3f0679698b900b7d64ddfc387c1773ac070571e8"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving","heading":"Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A68
The handbook uses interstate to mean a controlled-access highway with multiple lanes. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A68
Before entering an interstate, identify a gap in the nearest traffic lane. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A68
At an entrance ramp, wait for the broken-white-line portion, then adjust speed, signal and merge into a safe gap. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A68
On the interstate, maintain a steady traffic-compatible speed while obeying posted limits. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A68
Keep slower traffic right and avoid unnecessary lane changes; ordinarily remain right unless overtaking. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A68
Watch entrance ramps and, if safe, signal and move left to help entering traffic merge. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A68
Signal before changing lanes and check blind spots before passing. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A68
After missing an interstate exit, continue to the next exit rather than backing up or using an emergency crossover. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A68
Do not cross an interstate median. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A68
The manual lists forty miles per hour as the interstate minimum speed. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A68
Plan an exit early, signal and reach its proper lane at least a mile before the intended exit. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A69
For an interstate exit, slow after entering the deceleration lane and check the ramp's advised speed. [A69] [A68]
Source: [A69 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A69
After leaving the interstate, watch for two-way traffic and newly posted speed limits. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A69
Use headlights between sunset and sunrise. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A69
Turn on low beams as daylight fades so other drivers can see the vehicle; parking lamps alone are unlawful for driving. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A69
Switch off auxiliary driving lamps when approaching from ahead or behind at the same time headlights require dimming. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A69
Choose a night-driving speed that permits stopping within the illuminated roadway. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A69
Use high beams on open highways, but dim them for oncoming vehicles and when following within two hundred feet. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A69
If oncoming glare is blinding, look toward the right road edge instead of directly at the lights. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A69
Keep both sides of the windshield clean and move your gaze instead of staring into the headlight-lit spot. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A70
In rain, slow to match surface conditions; hydroplaning occurs when the tires ride on water instead of contacting the road. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A70
Rain may require disengaging cruise control; use low beams and increase the following gap. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A70
Do not enter a flooded roadway; turn around and find another route. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A70
Floodwater can conceal dips or a damaged road surface even when it appears shallow. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec13-F25 | anchor: A70
The manual warns that six inches of water can reach the underside of most passenger cars and cause stalling or lost control. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec13-F26 | anchor: A70
The manual warns that two feet of moving water can sweep away most vehicles, including SUVs and pickups. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec13-F27 | anchor: A70
If no alternate route exists around flooding, go to higher ground and wait for the water to recede; use extra caution at night. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec13-F28 | anchor: A70
In fog, use low beams, reduce speed and proceed with extreme caution. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec13-F29 | anchor: A70
The manual advises against travel on roads posted at forty miles per hour or more when visibility is below a quarter mile. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec13-F30 | anchor: A70
Small and high-profile vehicles are especially affected by wind; anticipate corrections after leaving shelter or meeting large vehicles. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec13-F31 | anchor: A70
Watch for high-wind advisories while travelling. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec13-F32 | anchor: A70
On snow or ice, slow down, increase following distance, clear the windows and make speed or direction changes gradually. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec13-F33 | anchor: A70
Do not use cruise control on snow or ice. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec13-F34 | anchor: A71
For snowy or icy conditions, the handbook tells non-ABS drivers to pump the brake pedal to avoid lockup; rolling tires are needed for steering. [A71] [A70]
Source: [A71 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec13-F35 | anchor: A71
For snowy or icy conditions with ABS, press firmly and do not pump the brakes. [A71] [A70]
Source: [A71 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec13-F36 | anchor: A71
On a slippery uphill climb, apply enough power to maintain speed without spinning the wheels. [A71] [A70]
Source: [A71 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec13-F37 | anchor: A71
The printed studded-tire season runs from November first to April first. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec13-F38 | anchor: A71
The manual advises against driving in blizzards because poor visibility, slippery surfaces and wind occur together. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> pdf-0071]

Misconceptions: Hands-free equipment can still distract; following distance increases with adversity; a missed interstate exit does not justify reversing.
Mnemonics: Prepare early, see clearly, leave space and stop driving when unfit.
Glossary: Hydroplaning is riding on water rather than pavement; ABS is antilock braking; visual, manual and cognitive distractions affect eyes, hands and attention.
Dynamic facts: Live contact details, services and variable fees are withheld from this stable inventory.
